key_insight: Free-stream forcing in hypersonic blunt-body boundary layers is amplified by a two-stage mechanism: a nose-region slow-down convection that boosts streamwise vorticity by O(√R), followed by downstream lift-up that drives streamwise velocity growth to O(R).
engineering_relevance: These receptivity mechanisms help predict and control non-modal disturbance growth in hypersonic boundary layers, which is important for transition management, thermal protection, and blunt-nose vehicle design.
method: High-Reynolds-number asymptotic analysis of the receptivity process
Reduced-order model derived from the identified amplification mechanisms
Comparison against SF-HLNS simulations across the downstream evolution
evidence_signal: The reduced model predictions agree well with shock-fitting harmonic linearised Navier–Stokes (SF-HLNS) calculations from the prior numerical framework.
watch_item: The reduced model is asymptotic and may lose accuracy outside the high-Reynolds-number blunt-body regime or when wall temperature/nose-radius effects move away from the validated range.
paper_title: Excitation of non-modal perturbations in hypersonic boundary layers by free stream forcing. Part II: asymptotic theory and key mechanisms
